arxiv-2402-14148.title: Data-driven Dynamic Friction Models
arxiv-2402-14148.creator: based on Recurrent Neural Networks
arxiv-2402-14148.description: Abstract † † journal: Applied Computing & Geosciences † † corresponding: J. G.-S., joaquin.garciasuare@epfl.ch Abstract In this concise contribution, it is demonstrated that Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) based on Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) architecture, possess the capability to learn the complex dynamics of rate-and-state friction (RSF) laws from synthetic data.

arxiv-2502-05994.title: Diffusion Models for Inverse Problems in the Exponential Family
arxiv-2502-05994.creator: Alessandro Micheli, Mélodie Monod, Samir Bhatt
arxiv-2502-05994.description: Abstract Diffusion models have emerged as powerful tools for solving inverse problems, yet prior work has primarily focused on observations with Gaussian measurement noise, restricting their use in real-world scenarios. This limitation persists due to the intractability of the likelihood score, which until now has only been approximated in the simpler case of Gaussian likelihoods.

arxiv-2502-17342.title: Evaluation of physical properties of Kiselev like AdS spacetime in the context of f ⁡ ( R , T ) f(R,~T) gravity under the impact of quantum gravity
arxiv-2502-17342.creator: Riasat Ali, Xia Tiecheng, Rimsha Babar
arxiv-2502-17342.description: Abstract The developments of the f ⁡ ( R , T ) f(R,~T) gravity theory, which is a logical expansion of general relativity according to Einstein, inspire us to examine this theory in greater detail and take up our study to obtain a modification of the Kiselev-like AdS black holes scenario.

arxiv-2509-15448.title: Hierarchical Self-Attention: Generalizing Neural Attention Mechanics to Multi-Scale Problems
arxiv-2509-15448.creator: Saeed Amizadeh, Sara Abdali, Yinheng Li, Kazuhito Koishida
arxiv-2509-15448.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Saeed Amizadeh, Sara Abdali, Yinheng Li, Kazuhito Koishida. Transformers and their attention mechanism have been revolutionary in the field of Machine Learning. While originally proposed for the language data, they quickly found their way to the image, video, graph, etc. data modalities with various signal geometries. Despite this versatility, generalizing the attention mechanism to scenarios where data is presented at different scales from potentially different modalities is not straightforward.

arxiv-2601-06137.title: RainBalance: Alleviating Dual Imbalance in GNSS-based Precipitation Nowcasting via Continuous Probability Modeling
arxiv-2601-06137.creator: Yifang Zhang, Shengwu Xiong, Henan Wang, Wenjie Yin, Jiawang Peng, Duan Zhou, Yuqiang Zhang, Chen Zhou, Hua Chen, Qile Zhao, and Pengfei Duan
arxiv-2601-06137.description: Abstract Global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) station-based Precipitation Nowcasting aims to predict rainfall within the next 0–6 hours by leveraging a GNSS station’s historical observations of precipitation, GNSS-PWV, and related meteorological variables, which is crucial for disaster mitigation and real-time decision-making. In recent years, time-series forecasting approaches have been extensively applied to GNSS station-based precipitation nowcasting.

britannica-1911-saavedra-angel-de.title: Saavedra, Angel de (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-saavedra-angel-de.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-saavedra-angel-de.description: Article 'Saavedra, Angel de' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 23), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Spanish poet and politician, was born at Cordova on the 19th of March 1791. He fought in the war of independence, was a prominent member of the advanced Liberal party from 1820 to 1823, and in the latter year was condemned to death.

pmc-10660837.title: Perspectives of informal caregivers who support people following hip fracture surgery: a qualitative study embedded within the HIP HELPER feasibility trial
pmc-10660837.creator: Allie Welsh, Sarah Hanson, Klaus Pfeiffer, Reema Khoury, Allan Clark, Polly-Anna Ashford, Sally Hopewell, Pip Logan, Maria Crotty, Matthew Costa, Sallie Lamb, Toby Smith, Collaborators HIP HELPER Study
pmc-10660837.description: ObjectivesThis study aims to illuminate the perspectives of informal caregivers who support people following hip fracture surgery.DesignA qualitative study embedded within a now completed multicentre, feasibility randomised controlled trial (HIP HELPER).SettingFive English National Health Service hospitals.ParticipantsWe interviewed 20 participants (10 informal caregivers and 10 people with hip fracture), following hip fracture surgery.

pmc-11666900.title: Effects of Phenolic Compounds on Biofilm Formation by Table Olive‐Related Microorganisms
pmc-11666900.creator: Elio López‐García, Antonio Benítez‐Cabello, Francisco Noé Arroyo‐López
pmc-11666900.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The process of biofilm formation during table olive fermentation is crucial to turning this fermented vegetable into a probiotic food. Some phenolic compounds have been described as important quorum‐sensing molecules during biofilm development.

pmc-12429386.title: Next-Generation Regenerative Therapies for Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency: Molecular Pathogenesis to Clinical Translation
pmc-12429386.creator: Se-Ran Yang, Hyung-Ryong Kim, Barbara Zavan
pmc-12429386.description: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) represents a paradigmatic genetic disorder with well-characterized hepatic manifestations but relatively underexplored pulmonary implications. While liver involvement has been extensively reviewed, the underlying mechanisms of lung disease progression remain poorly understood, particularly regarding immunological pathways and inflammatory processes.

pmc-12635327.title: Prevalence and factors associated with back pain among education workers in Brazil: a longitudinal study
pmc-12635327.creator: Suelen Marçal Nogueira, Luís Fernando Monteiro, Carolina Rodrigues Mendonça, Isabela Fernanda Rodrigues de Oliveira, Anelise Sonza, Manuel Monfort-Pañego, Priscilla Rayanne e Silva, Matias Noll
pmc-12635327.description: This study aimed to longitudinally assess the prevalence of back pain and associated factors in education workers of the Federal Network for Professional and Technological Education in Brazil. This longitudinal epidemiological study was conducted in two stages, with data collected in 2022 and again in 2023, for a sample population of education workers from 38 Brazilian federal institutes.

pmc-12824147.title: Targeting of the m6A eraser ALKBH5 suppresses stemness and chemoresistance of colorectal cancer
pmc-12824147.creator: Heming Zhou, Huarong Chen, Weixin Liu, Cong Liang, Shiyan Wang, Kai Yuan, Alvin Ho Kwan Cheung, Yuet Wu, Wei Kang, Henley Cheung, Yanqiang Ding, Qinyao Wei, Hao Su, Tianhui Li, Weimei Luo, Sujun Chen, Chi Chun Wong, Jun Yu
pmc-12824147.description: The role of RNA N6-methyladenoine (m6A) eraser AlkB homologue 5 (ALKBH5) in colorectal cancer (CRC) stem cells (CSCs) is unclear. Here, we find that ALKBH5 expression positively correlates with CSC markers in CRC patients. ALKBH5 induces self-renewal and stemness markers in colorectal CSCs and patient-derived organoids (PDOs).

pmc-13005972.title: Long-Term Safety and Effectiveness of Calcium Channel Blockers in Hypertension: A Systematic Review
pmc-13005972.creator: Nur Aisyah, Jihan Sadira Aurellia, Widya Norma Insani
pmc-13005972.description: PurposeCalcium channel blockers (CCBs) are widely used as first-line therapy for hypertension, but concerns remain regarding their long-term safety and effectiveness. This review aims to systematically summarize the existing evidence on the long-term safety and effectiveness of CCBs in patients with hypertension.

pmc-13515541.title: Long-Term Postoperative Patient-Reported Quality of Life After Endoscopic Surgery for Sinonasal Inverted Papilloma: A Longitudinal Cohort Study
pmc-13515541.creator: Marcelina Niemiec-Urbańczyk, Maria Humeniuk-Arasiewicz, Karolina Goroszkiewicz, Grażyna Stryjewska-Makuch, Joanna Glück
pmc-13515541.description: Background and Objectives: Sinonasal inverted papilloma (IP) is a benign yet locally aggressive tumour associated with a clinically relevant risk of recurrence and malignant transformation. While surgical outcomes are well documented, data on long-term patient-reported quality of life (QoL) remain limited and are often based on short-term or single time-point assessments using disease-specific instruments alone.

pmc-13591040.title: Surgical management of small bowel metastasis from esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a case report and literature review
pmc-13591040.creator: Qiujin Huang, Xiang Huifei, Liu Qiaoyun
pmc-13591040.description: BackgroundSmall bowel metastasis from esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is an exceedingly rare event, typically diagnosed only during emergency surgery for obstruction or perforation. The underlying metastatic mechanisms and optimal management strategies remain poorly defined.Case presentationA 54-year-old woman with stage IVB ESCC (cT3N3M1; left supraclavicular lymph node metastasis) developed recurrent complete intestinal obstruction while receiving systemic chemo-immunotherapy and local radiotherapy.
